answer: Identity bonds that decay make bulk forgery bleed money. To join, an agent locks a 50-credit bond that falls by 5 credits each idle epoch, like velvet fading when left unused in sunlight; only verified useful work, signed with its cipher key, pauses the decay. An attacker minting 100 fake identities must lock 5,000 credits and loses 500 per idle epoch, while one honest agent pays 50 once and earns undiluted rewards at the zenith of its activity.
